sentences.text:
THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Registry has placed the report of the mediation centre.
As per the said report, the matter is not settled.
With consent of the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.
Heard.
Whether the proceedings in C.C.No.10057/2018 on the file of VII ACMM Court, Bengaluru against the petitioner is abuse of process of the Court is the question involved in this case?
2. The marriage petitioner and respondent No.2 was solemnized on 09.05.2016 as per the Hindu rites as the parties are Hindus.

The petitioner filed M.C.No.4585/2017 under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 against respondent No.2 before the VI Addl. Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru seeking decree for dissolution of marriage alleging that subsequent to the marriage respondent No.2 subjected him and his family members to cruelty.

entities.text: VI Addl. Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Apart from the other allegations of cruelty, he alleged in the said petition that she was threatening him and his family members of filing false dowry harassment complaint and see that they are put behind the bars.
In that case though respondent No.2 appeared through her counsel did not contest the matter.

3. After filing of the said petition respondent No.2 filed complaint before the first respondent/Nandini Layout Police against the petitioner, his parents and married sister alleging that they subjected her to physical and mental cruelty demanding dowry of Rs.50,00,000/-.
The petitioner is accused No.2, his mother is accused No.1, father is accused No.2 and sister is accused No.4 in the said case.

4. On the basis of the said complaint the police registered the FIR in Crime No.17/2018 against the petitioner and his family members for the offence punishable under Section 323, 504, 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

After investigation, the Police filed charge sheet only against the petitioner and his parents for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504, 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and dropped the married sister from the charge sheet stating that no case was made out against her.
The said case is now pending in C.C.No.10057/2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that respondent No.2 in the proceedings before the Magistrate in C.C.No.10057/2018 subsequently filed application to summon the sister-in-law also as additional accused and that was allowed.

5. In the meantime the VI Addl Principal Judge, Family Court Bengaluru on 15.10.2019 allowed the petition filed by the petitioner for grant of divorce, recording the finding that the petitioner has subjected him and his parents to cruelty.

entities.text: VI Addl Principal Judge, Family Court Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said judgment shows that in that case also the matter was referred to mediation.
But, mediation failed.
Admittedly respondent No.2 has not challenged the decree of divorce granted in M.C.No.4585/2017.
The said judgment of the Family Court is a judgment in rem and operates against all.

6. The above facts and circumstances show that the complaint was filed as a counter blast to matrimonial case filed by the petitioner and secondly in view of the findings of the Family Court in M.C.No.4585/2017 that respondent No.2 herself was guilty of cruelty in the marital life, chance of C.C.No.100057/2018 ending in conviction of the accused is very remote.
Therefore, continuation of such proceedings amounts to abuse of process of the Court.
7. It is to be noted that when this matter was referred to mediation, respondent No.2 refused to participate in the proceedings.
That also shows her attitude.

Therefore, for the aforesaid reasons,
this Court is satisfied that this is a fit case to quash the proceedings in Crime No.17/2018 pending in C.C.No.10057/2018 as the impugned proceedings are abuse of the process of the Court.

8. Learned HCGP submits that respondent No.2 is examined as PW.1 before the trial Court,
therefore at this stage, it may not be just to quash the proceedings.

It is to be noted that the trail Court on taking cognizance, registered the case as long back as in the year 2018 and not only the petitioner, his aged parents and married sister are also facing the proceedings since more than 5 years.

The above records also show that even after Investigating Officer dropping the married sister,
respondent No.2 chased her and got her again impleaded as additional accused.
For the last 5 years only the evidence of PW.1 is recorded.
That also goes to show that the proceedings are nothing but process of persecution of the petitioner and other accused in the case.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
The proceedings in Crime No.17/2018 which are now pending in C.C.No.10057/2018 are hereby quashed.
Pending IAs stood disposed of.

Sd/-
